title: Does knowing the slope remove noise?
hook: Separate parameter spread from noise of one new outcome.

doesNotKnow: At x=2, slope 0/1 has weights .2/.8; independent noise is ±1 equally. Does knowing the slope remove all outcome variance?

objective: Compute the aleatoric vs epistemic finite model and explain its changed countercase and stated boundary.

claims.text:
2. aleatoric-vs-epistemic

Target / packet: ai-aleatoric-vs-epistemic · P1. Prerequisites: ai:bayesian-posterior-lines.

Nearest / distinct payoff: bayesian-posterior-lines → ai-bayesian-posterior-lines. Posterior lines alone vary parameters; here independent outcome noise persists after parameter uncertainty is removed.

Finite primary model: Use slopes 0/1 with posterior [.2,.8] and independent observation noise±1 equally. At x=2 slope uncertainty variance=.64 plus noise variance 1 gives observation variance 1.64. Fix slope 1 with certainty and variance becomes 1.

Countercase and mathematical boundary: At x=0 slope contribution 0 but noise remains 1. This is a stipulated additive model: averaging repeated measurements can reduce noise of the mean, even though noise of each new outcome remains 1.

Predict and recall transfer: Predict which variance survives knowing the slope; recall x=3 parameter contribution 1.44 and total 2.44.

Required observable evidence: Separate uncertainty of latent mean from spread of a new observation; never use one undifferentiated confidence badge.

Source obligation: [Rasmussen–Williams author textbook, chapter2](https://gaussianprocess.org/gpml/chapters/RW2.pdf), acquired body, §2.1 and eq2.5 posterior normalization. This finite two-slope likelihood is locally declared, not the book Gaussian example; latent/observation uncertainty decomposition follows the explicit independent local construction.
